departure_points.name: Shady Camp boat ramps (Mary River National Park)
departure_points.detail: Ramps on both the freshwater (billabong) side and the saltwater side of the Shady Camp barrage, plus picnic areas and toilets. The saltwater ramp gives access down the tidal river to the mouth.

departure_points.name: Corroboree Billabong boat ramp
departure_points.detail: Public boat ramp 108 km east of Darwin off the Arnhem Highway (partly unsealed access road, open April to December), launching into about 45 km of fishable water.

departure_points.name: Rockhole boat ramp
departure_points.detail: Launch point off Point Stuart Road in Mary River National Park giving access to the Mary River channels; the Mary River Wetlands Cruise also departs here.

departure_points.name: Darwin hotel pick-up
departure_points.detail: Darwin-based guides collect clients from their accommodation at about 5am in a 4WD and drive out along the Arnhem Highway, returning mid to late afternoon.

departure_points.name: Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge
departure_points.detail: Lodge on Point Stuart Road, 20 minutes' drive (about 20 km) from the Shady Camp ramp; base for the lodge's own guided trips and for run-off packages run by Darwin guides.

grounds.name: Shady Camp billabong (above the barrage)
grounds.detail: Permanent freshwater billabong; after the floodwaters drop it fishes for barramundi, saratoga and tarpon by casting the lily-lined banks or trolling edges and rock bars.

grounds.name: Shady Camp barrage (salt/fresh divide)
grounds.detail: Built in the late 1980s (1987 per Tourism Top End) over a natural rock bar to stop saltwater pushing into the wetlands while letting floodwater out and fish migrate. Fresh water meets tidal salt water here, and at the end of the wet mullet gather to feed and barra follow them. It is also a land-based hotspot (special hook rules apply within 100 m).

grounds.name: Sampan Creek and Tommycut Creek mouths, Chambers Bay
grounds.detail: Below the barrage the Mary splits into two estuaries that flow into Chambers Bay (Van Diemen Gulf). From February to May big barra are caught trolling both creek mouths and along the coast wherever run-off pours in; the mangrove feeder creeks are cast on spring tides.

grounds.name: Chambers Bay shoals and reefs
grounds.detail: About 10 km north of the Sampan Creek mouth, reachable from the Shady Camp ramp on neap tides: black jewfish (10–15 kg average), golden snapper, blue salmon and cod. Time departure and return with the top of the tide.

grounds.name: Corroboree Billabong and Hardies Lagoon
grounds.detail: A large lily-fringed billabong system west of the national park, about an hour or so from Darwin, consistently good for dry-season barramundi plus saratoga and tarpon; a wildlife trip as much as a fishing trip.

grounds.name: Corroboree and Rockhole billabongs
grounds.detail: Together these inland waterways stretch about 20 km and hold tarpon, saratoga and barramundi.

species_seasons.when: Run-off: late February to May (peak March–April)
species_seasons.detail: Floodplains drain into the river and creeks, flushing bait; the biggest fish of the year are taken downstream of the Shady Camp barrage and at the creek mouths. Fish of up to 1.4 m are landed each year in the Mary River wetlands.
Billabong fishing (Shady Camp billabong, Corroboree) by trolling or casting the lilies; generally smaller fish, more consistent days.
Big barra move back to the river mouths to breed and come back on the bite; fished on neap tides when the water clears.
Possible between monsoon storms; neap tides on the salt side of Shady Camp can produce big fish, but Shady Camp road access is 4WD only.

species_seasons.when: Later in the run-off and in the build-up
species_seasons.detail: Arrive in the river later in the run-off; double and triple hook-ups occur.
Shallow reefs a few kilometres off the river mouth in Chambers Bay.

rules.rule: Mary River Fish Management Zone: possession limit of 3 barramundi per person (minimum 55 cm) and 3 king threadfin per person, plus a restriction on barramundi over 90 cm (one per vessel). Check the NT page for the exact size wording before publishing.
rules.source: https://nt.gov.au/marine/recreational-fishing/rules-for-fishing-in-specific-areas/mary-river-fish-management-zone (read via search result; the page blocks automated fetching)

rules.rule: The 3-barramundi limit is a possession limit (what you hold at any time), not a daily fishing limit.
Cast nets and drag nets may not be used or carried in the Mary River Fish Management Zone.
Within 100 m of the Shady Camp barrage wall you may only fish with a lure or fly on a single-point hook; bait and double or treble hooks are banned.

No current seasonal closure: the Mary River downstream of the Shady Camp barrage used to close from 1 October to 31 January, but a 2014 legislative change opened it to year-round recreational fishing.

An NT Parks Visitor Pass is needed to enter Mary River National Park (separate from Kakadu and Uluru passes; NT residents exempt). Camping at Shady Camp and Couzens Lookout must be booked and paid online beforehand.

Crocodile safety: the Mary River has up to 15 saltwater crocodiles per kilometre, one of the highest densities in the world. Be Crocwise: don't swim, keep back from the water's edge and watch the crocs from the Shady Camp viewing platform.

getting_there.detail: From Darwin take the Stuart Highway, then turn left onto the Arnhem Highway; Mary River National Park is about an hour on sealed roads. The Mary River area is about 150 km (1.5 hours) east of Darwin and 140 km (1.5 hours) west of Jabiru.
Shady Camp is about 200 km from Darwin: around 1 hour 40 minutes by car, or about 2 hours towing a boat. In the wet season access is 4WD only.
Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge is about 2 hours from Darwin or the airport, sealed nearly all the way (the last 7 km is well-maintained gravel), and suits 2WD; Shady Camp is 20 minutes on.
Corroboree Billabong is 108 km east of Darwin off the Arnhem Highway (partly unsealed, open April to December).
Rockhole is off Point Stuart Road via the Bird Billabong turn-off. NT Tourism says it is about an hour from Darwin; Tourism Top End says about two hours.

notes.detail: Shady Camp lets one trip fish both a freshwater billabong and a tidal saltwater river, depending on tide and season.
The Wulwulam people are the traditional owners of the Mary River area. John McDouall Stuart named the river in 1862, and Point Stuart is where his expedition reached the sea.

Accommodation where charters are based: Point Stuart Wilderness Lodge (lodge rooms, safari tents and camping; open 26 February to 30 September) hosts run-off packages. Mary River Wilderness Retreat (4642 Arnhem Highway, Mount Bundey; 110 km from Darwin) is a build-up base for some guides.
Houseboats and fishing dinghies can be hired, and professional guides work most of the year, including from motherships during the run-off.
Mary River National Park covers Rockhole, Couzens Lookout, Brian Creek and Jimmy Creek monsoon forests, Point Stuart Coastal Reserve, Shady Camp, Mistake Billabong and the Hardies 4WD track.

faq.q: When is the best time to fish the Mary River for barramundi?
faq.a: The run-off, from late February to May, is the peak for big barra below the Shady Camp barrage and at the creek mouths. The build-up (September to mid-December) is the other big-fish window. In the dry season (roughly May to September) the billabongs fish consistently for barra and saratoga.

faq.q: How far is the Mary River from Darwin?
faq.a: Corroboree Billabong is about 108 km (roughly an hour or more) east of Darwin and Shady Camp is about 200 km (around 1 hour 40 minutes), both via the Stuart and Arnhem Highways.

faq.q: Can I do a Mary River fishing trip as a day trip from Darwin?
faq.a: Yes. Several guides pick up from Darwin accommodation at about 5am and fish Corroboree Billabong or Shady Camp, returning mid to late afternoon. Run-off trips are usually multi-day and lodge-based.

faq.q: How many barramundi can I keep?
faq.a: In the Mary River Fish Management Zone the possession limit is 3 barramundi per person (minimum 55 cm), with extra limits on fish over 90 cm. It applies to fish in your possession, not a daily catch.

faq.q: Can I fish from the bank at Shady Camp?
faq.a: Yes, the barrage is a well-known land-based spot on both sides. Within 100 m of the wall only lures or flies with a single-point hook are allowed, and crocodile numbers are very high, so keep well back from the edge.

faq.q: Do I need a park pass?
faq.a: Visitors need an NT Parks Visitor Pass for Mary River National Park (from $10 per adult for a day). NT residents are exempt. Campsites must be booked online before you arrive.

faq.q: Is there a closed season on the Mary River?
faq.a: Not for recreational fishing downstream of Shady Camp. The old 1 October–31 January closure was removed in 2014, but zone-specific limits and gear rules still apply.

faq.q: Can I get to Shady Camp in the wet season?
faq.a: Only by 4WD. Corroboree Billabong's access road is listed as open April to December.

departure_points.name: Katherine River spots near town
departure_points.detail: Knotts Crossing, Donkey Camp and the low-level bridge, plus Galloping Jacks west of town.

departure_points.name: Big Horse Creek boat ramp (Victoria River)
departure_points.detail: About 7 km west of Timber Creek; cement ramp usable year-round, with toilets, fireplaces and limited drinking water. The starting point for most Victoria River anglers.

departure_points.name: Roper Bar
departure_points.detail: The crossing separating the Roper River's salt and fresh sections; most fishing is east (downstream) of it. Caravan park, camping and lodge accommodation are available.

grounds.name: Katherine River
grounds.detail: Holds barramundi and sooty grunter; fishing after the wet can be good close to town.

grounds.name: Victoria River near Timber Creek and the Baines River
grounds.detail: Big-tide river; the tide reaches only a few kilometres above Timber Creek, and some huge barramundi are caught near the town each year. Locals run downstream by boat to the Baines River.

grounds.name: Upper Victoria River (Victoria River bridge and gorge)
grounds.detail: Freshwater holes including the Victoria River Gorge; further upstream the river becomes segmented pools that can be fished from shore and hold surprisingly large barramundi. Policeman's Point near Timber Creek is a bank-fishing spot.

grounds.name: Roper River (tidal section)
grounds.detail: Lure fishing for barra in the run-off and live bait through the dry; black jewfish, threadfin salmon, giant trevally, golden snapper and mud crabs in the tidal reaches.

species_seasons.when: Neap tides, late March to late May
species_seasons.detail: Can be caught all year, but the end of the monsoon (run-off) on neap tides, when the water is clearest, is best.
Spots close to town fish well once the tropical summer is over.
Most fishing is east of Roper Bar.

rules.rule: Estuarine (saltwater) crocodiles live in the Victoria River area; follow all safety signs around waterways.
The lower tidal section of the Daly River (north-west of Katherine) is closed to fishing from 1 October to 31 January.
Check NT bag limits and restricted zones before fishing, for example in the free NT Fishing Mate app.

getting_there.detail: Katherine is about 300 km south of Darwin on the Stuart Highway.
The Victoria River Crossing is 194 km west of Katherine and Timber Creek about 250 km, both on the Victoria Highway; Timber Creek is roughly halfway between Katherine and Kununurra.

notes.detail: The Victoria (the 'Vic') is the Territory's biggest river and flows into the Joseph Bonaparte Gulf.
NT Tourism says guided fishing tours and boat hire are available at the Victoria River Roadhouse and Timber Creek, but no current, verifiable operator could be identified this round.

faq.q: Can you catch barramundi in the Katherine River?
faq.a: Yes. The Katherine River holds barramundi and sooty grunter, and spots near town such as Knotts Crossing, Donkey Camp and the low-level bridge can fish well after the wet.

faq.q: When is the best time to fish the Victoria River?
faq.a: On neap tides between late March and late May, as the wet season ends, although barra are caught all year.

faq.q: Where do I launch a boat on the Victoria River?
faq.a: Most anglers use the Big Horse Creek boat ramp, about 7 km west of Timber Creek.

departure_points.name: King Ash Bay Fishing Club boat ramp
departure_points.detail: Two-lane ramp on the McArthur River, about 40 km from Borroloola (NT Tourism says around 50 km), giving access to hundreds of kilometres of mangrove rivers and creeks and the Sir Edward Pellew Islands.

departure_points.name: Borroloola ramps
departure_points.detail: Public boat ramps near the Council works yard and at Rocky Creek in Borroloola, plus Mule Creek on Bing Bong Station.

departure_points.name: Darwin (seaplane to a Roper River mothership)
departure_points.detail: Australian Sportfishing Charters flies guests from Darwin to its mothership on the Roper River by Grumman Mallard seaplane (about 2 hours).

grounds.name: McArthur River and delta
grounds.detail: Sheltered, mangrove-lined river and creeks with barramundi plus mangrove jack, golden snapper (fingermark), black jewfish, threadfin and blue salmon, grunter and queenfish; mud crabs too. There is a large tidal range and mud flats at low tide.

grounds.name: Sir Edward Pellew Islands
grounds.detail: Reefs and rock outcrops around North (Barranyi NP), Vanderlin, West and Centre Islands hold coral trout, nannygai, mackerel and emperor; billfish are found in good numbers close to the islands.

grounds.name: Roper River
grounds.detail: Navigable for about 170 km into the Gulf of Carpentaria. Barra are sight-cast on the sand flats on the making tide and fished in deep bends and holes on the falling tide; also threadfin salmon, golden snapper, mangrove jack and saratoga.

grounds.name: Limmen Bight, Cox and Towns Rivers
grounds.detail: Barramundi fishing along the 4WD Nathan River road between Roper Bar and Cape Crawford; the Limmen Bight River also offers mud crabs.

species_seasons.detail: The best barra periods at King Ash Bay, though barra are caught all year and some prefer the cooler dry season.
The run-off concentrates fish on the flats and in deep holes; the dry season brings clearer water for sight-fishing.

rules.rule: Recreational fishers and fishing tour operators don't need a permit to fish the waters of the McArthur River and Sir Edward Pellew Islands region, but the islands are Yanyuwa country, so respect cultural access rules (Northern Land Council).
The King Ash Bay club encourages careful release of barramundi over 85 cm (breeding stock). Swimming is not recommended because of crocodiles.

getting_there.detail: Borroloola is about 12 hours' drive south-east of Darwin, near the Queensland border; from Katherine it is about 7 hours via the sealed but single-lane Carpentaria Highway.

King Ash Bay is about 50 km past Borroloola; the last 21 km is dirt, fine for 2WD in the dry but flooded and boggy in the wet. Airnorth flies to the McArthur River Mine, about an hour's drive from King Ash Bay.

notes.detail: King Ash Bay Fishing Club is a small self-sufficient township on 500 acres beside the McArthur River, with camping, a bar and grill, a fuel station and mini-mart, houseboats and fishing tours. It swells with visitors each dry season from around Easter.
Limmen River Fishing Camp and King Ash Bay are popular bases for anglers.

faq.q: When is the best time to fish King Ash Bay?
faq.a: For barramundi, the build-up (September–December) and the run-off (March–May). The dry season (from around Easter) has the most comfortable weather and is the busiest time.

faq.q: Do I need a permit to fish around the Sir Edward Pellew Islands?
faq.a: No fishing-access permit is needed for recreational fishers in the McArthur River and Pellew Islands waters, but respect Yanyuwa cultural sites and park rules (Barranyi National Park is boat access only).
